# Appeal of Denial — Lower Back Disc Surgery/Decompression (CPT 63030)

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-24
**Reference Number:** POC-1C51E72E1E-65750
**Member:** Skyler Ellison
**Member ID:** W240749705
**Plan:** PacificSource Health Plans (Commercial/ACA), Idaho
**Governing Policy:** Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery, https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/spine-surgery-2025-11-15-updated-2026-01-01/ (effective 2025-11-15, updated 2026-01-01)

Dear PacificSource Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of the lower back disc surgery/decompression (CPT 63030) that my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has determined I need. The denial notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking that you reconsider this decision, because my records show that I have met the plan's own published criteria for this surgery.

## How my records meet the plan's criteria

**1. Conservative management combining physical therapy and a complementary treatment**

The guideline states:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My records show I completed 24 supervised physical therapy visits over 10 weeks (2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03), focused on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. In addition, I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-30, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. This combination satisfies both the physical therapy requirement and the complementary treatment requirement.

**2. Participation in a tailored program with documented compliance**

The guideline states:

> "Participation in a patient-specific or tailored program Initial active instruction by MD/DO/PT with redemonstration of patient ability to perform exercises Compliance (documented or by clinician attestation on follow-up evaluation)..."

My physical therapy was a supervised, patient-specific program (core stabilization and lumbar flexibility), and my completion of all 24 visits is documented in the discharge note, which reflects compliance with the plan of care.

**3. Clinical reevaluation in reasonable proximity to the anticipated date of service**

The guideline states:

> "Clinical reevaluation must be done in reasonable proximity to the anticipated date of service such that the patient's condition would be unlikely to change by the date of service."

My MRI of the lumbar spine was performed on 2026-07-28, close to the end of my physical therapy course, and showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. Nothing in my records indicates any change in my condition since that evaluation.

**4. Failure of conservative management — all required elements**

The guideline states:

> "Failure of conservative management requires ALL the following:"

and

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My records show all of these elements: a full 10-week course of physical therapy was completed; NSAIDs and a corticosteroid injection produced only inadequate or temporary relief; and my surgeon is now recommending decompression surgery as a more invasive option. My physical therapy discharge note documents my compliance with the program.

**5. Significant pain and functional impairment**

The guideline states:

> "For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records document that I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes and have radicular pain extending into my right calf, along with positive provocative testing and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level on exam. My chart does not appear to include a specific numeric pain rating; if one was recorded elsewhere in my chart, it should read [patient-reported pain score, e.g., X/10 — to be confirmed from chart]. The functional limitations documented, however, are consistent with the significant impairment this criterion describes.

## Summary

Taken together, my records show a full course of physical therapy, use of medication and an injection as complementary conservative treatment, a recent MRI confirming nerve root compression, ongoing significant functional limitation, and no meaningful improvement despite these treatments — all of which map directly onto the plan's own published criteria for conservative management and its failure. I am asking PacificSource to review this evidence again and reverse the denial.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-20** (180 days from the date of the denial notice).

I am submitting this appeal by: [mail / fax to 541-225-3628 / electronically through InTouch "Ask a Question" / email to NewAppeal@PacificSource.com] — PacificSource's own materials note that electronic submissions are processed more quickly.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed from me or from Dr. Lindqvist's office to complete this review.

Sincerely,

[Skyler Ellison]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
